members.name: Robyn Seglem
members.title: English Language Arts
members.bio: Dr. Robyn Seglem teaches English Language Arts at CSST. She spent nine years teaching middle and high school ELA and seventeen years in teacher education, preparing and mentoring the next generation of educators. A nationally board-certified teacher, she co-chaired the team that revised the second edition of the National Board for Professional Teaching Standards' Five Core Propositions, and she is the co-author of two books on literacy instruction and social action. She builds classrooms where collaboration drives learning and every student is challenged to grow.

members.name: Darren Kelley
members.title: Mathematics
members.bio: Darren connects math to real-world problems in technology and business, making abstract concepts concrete through project-based learning. His students leave understanding not just how to solve equations, but why math is the language of every industry.

members.name: Ken King
members.title: Math, Aviation & Leadership
members.bio: Ken teaches math, aviation, and leadership, bringing military aviation, behavioral science, and human factors engineering to CSST. He previously served as a Course Director for Aviation Psychology and Human Factors at the U.S. Air Force Academy and as a Research Director for the Warfighter Effectiveness Research Center. He is the only military officer ever awarded both Navy Aerospace Experimental Psychology and Air Force pilot wings. Ken earned his undergraduate degree in Architecture from the University of Illinois and his master's in Human Factors from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University.

members.name: Caleb Ulliman
members.title: Science
members.bio: Caleb teaches science through inquiry and experimentation, connecting curriculum to the aerospace and technology sectors right outside CSST's doors. His lab approach builds the critical-thinking skills that define every great engineer.

members.name: Courtnie Schobert
members.title: Science
members.bio: Courtnie teaches science at CSST with a hands-on, project-based approach shaped by her time teaching at a trade school. She holds a Bachelor of Innovation from the University of Colorado Colorado Springs and serves as a Teacher Liaison for the Space Foundation, connecting classroom learning to real-world science and exploration. Outside of school, she enjoys spending time outdoors with her daughter.

members.name: Michael Bunch
members.title: Social Studies & Leadership
members.bio: Michael Bunch teaches World History, U.S. History, Civics, and Leadership. He designs rigorous, standards-aligned curriculum and brings a veteran's experience mentoring young adults and building collaborative teams. He earned his Ph.D. in Modern European History from the University of Colorado Boulder, focusing on migration, citizenship, and genocide. A former U.S. Army logistics officer, he has taught for eight years at the university and high school levels.

members.name: Molly Smith
members.title: Business & Entrepreneurship
members.bio: Molly Smith teaches Business, Personal Finance, and Workplace Readiness. She founded Republic of Paws, a pet retail and service business, in 2009, and previously taught Government, Economics, and Personal Finance at James Irwin Charter Schools. She focuses on financial literacy, professional skills, and the character students need for life after high school.

members.name: John Sellers
members.title: Business, Future Ready & PE
members.bio: John Sellers teaches Principles of Finance, Future Ready, and PE. He spent ten years as a Research Physiologist in the Army, leading research at three Army medical research laboratories, and earlier worked as an auditor with the U.S. Government Accountability Office. He holds a B.S. in accounting and an M.S. and Ph.D. in Health and Human Performance, along with university teaching experience and two years directing a federally accredited training program for military and law enforcement.

members.name: Jerard Carney
members.title: Computer Science
members.bio: Jerard Carney is the Lead Computer Science Instructor at CSST. With degrees in Artificial Intelligence Programming and Human-Computer Interaction, he builds learning experiences that push students to think, adapt, and get comfortable being uncomfortable. A former U.S. Army medic and EMT, he is guided by his motto, “Hic Servire” — “Here to Serve.” He wants school to be a proving ground where students can take risks and rise again. As he puts it: “Develop and fail here, before the world marks you.”
